scope: PROP-FLOOD-06.v3 (registry/proposals/flood_outlet_coping.json): one method-domain (M) proposal for a community flood-readout application (FloodConnect), via the governed proposals-lane intake process -- NOT promoted into registry/CANONICAL.json. Builds on the v2 ACK (parent chain, s_band fix, full_tier totality, g_U(t) discipline, unit-resolution defaults -- unchanged by this pass). This v3 pass is driven by (a) founder instruction 2026-09-27 (verbatim: "ทำทั้งหมดให้ระดับโลก แต่พอใช้ได้แม้ข้อมูลไม่ครบ อย่าลืมว่าระบบนี้ออกมาสำหรับวิกฤต บางอย่างมันอาจไม่สมบูรณ์ ขอแค่ข้อมูลจริงแม้เล็กที่สุดในบางสถานการณ์ก็ยังดี" -- build it world-class but usable even with incomplete data, since this system serves a crisis) and (b) a read-only falsifier backtest run in the sibling repo thailand_flood_kg (docs/BACKTEST_PROP_FLOOD_06_v0.md, RELAYED -- this repo did not conduct that backtest, only records its findings; thailand_flood_kg itself was not modified, per this task's scope). v3 AMENDMENTS: (1) the no-pump contradiction the backtest found (AYUTTHAYA_BANGBAN REFUSED 320/320 rows via ZERO_CAPACITY_NONZERO_INFLOW despite R_H/F_H resolving, because NO_PUMPS_IN_UNIT forces D_H:=0 and the literal min(D_H,R_H) always collapses to 0, contradicting this proposal's own worked-instantiation table) is fixed by a new total function C_H(U) (definitions.C_H(U); Coq `c_h`): NO_PUMPS_IN_UNIT with R_H resolved => C_H:=R_H (terms_present={R}); pumps declared but outlet capacity unknown => C_H:=D_H (terms_present={D}, a PARTIAL flag, not a refusal); both resolved => min(D_H,R_H) unchanged from v1/v2; neither resolved => still REFUSED (OUTLET_CAPACITY_UNKNOWN), the one genuinely non-resolvable case. (2) A graceful PARTIAL mode is added per the founder's rule that a tier must be returned whenever ANY real input exists, refusal reserved for when NONE does: readout_classes.mode in {FULL, PARTIAL, LR}, built on a new 7-component coverage vector cov(U) = (rain_obs, rain_fcst, canal_level_vs_lines, river_flow_vs_cap, dam_release, pumps_state, upstream_inflow), each in {present, stale, absent}. LR now fires only when cov(U) is entirely absent/stale; FULL is the unchanged v2 ledger path (now reading C_H(U) in place of the old literal min); PARTIAL is a new declared promoter_table (readout_classes.promoter_table, adopted RELAYED-derived-convention from thailand_flood_kg docs/knowledge/TIER_THRESHOLDS_RATIONALE.md's own WMO/UNDRR/Japan-keikai/UK-EA/US-NWS/DDPM-synthesized calibration pass) evaluated as a max over whichever promoters' required cov(U) component is present, carrying based_on/missing/coverage_score (a plain MEASURED count, never a probability) on every PARTIAL readout. A worked example (Hat Yai, only rain_obs + canal_level_vs_lines present, mode PARTIAL, tier L3, coverage_score 2/7) is added to both the JSON (worked_example_partial_hatyai_v3) and the MD. (3) S_H/T_act band VALUES themselves are explicitly UNCHANGED -- no silent tuning; the backtest's BANGKOK_EAST finding (92.5% overall REFUSED across 1676 rows; 126 non-REFUSED rows, all BANGKOK_EAST, 100.0% miss rate n=126; S_H degenerate at exactly 0.00 on both flooded and non-flooded days in that scenario) is recorded verbatim as an OPEN calibration note explicitly stating that no specific band shift is licensed by this finding, since a degenerate S_H (0.00 for both classes) cannot be separated by ANY band boundary -- the miss is attributed to the same C_H(U)/input-resolution gap this pass fixes, not to threshold placement. (4) coq/canonical/PROP_FLOOD_06_outlet_coping_tier.v extended with c_h (the C_H(U) case split), promoter_max (a total fold over a finite promoter list, absent/stale promoters excluded from the max rather than defaulting to a level), promote_one (the vulnerable-unit +1 rule, capped at L5, never promotes LR), and full_tier_v3 (the mode-selecting top-level function reusing v2's full_tier unchanged for the FULL branch) -- all new theorems proved (c_h_total, c_h_none_iff_no_pumps_and_no_outlet, promoter_max_total, promote_one_total, promote_one_never_creates_LR, promote_one_LR_is_noop, full_tier_v3_total, tier_level6_v3_eq_dec, cov_all_absent_is_always_LR) alongside the unchanged v2 theorems. Proposal bumped to v3 with a version_history entry and a new registry/LINEAGE.jsonl entry (code PROP-FLOOD-06, event revised). SEPARATELY, this pass also fixed a pre-existing bookkeeping error found while reading the v2 lineage entry: the LAST registry/LINEAGE.jsonl entry (the v1->v2 revision) had its `code` field literally set to the shared canonical-placeholder string "weld/M.??.v1" -- identical to the placeholder every other PROP-FLOOD-01..05b proposal's own `code` field carries (a legitimate, repo-wide convention meaning 'not yet canonically assigned, pending issue #11'). But a LINEAGE entry keyed on that shared placeholder cannot uniquely identify WHICH proposal was revised, since 01/02/03/05a/05b all use the identical string; the entry's own prose disambiguated it only informally. This has been corrected to `code: "PROP-FLOOD-06"` (the proposal's own stable identifier, per AGENTS.md's own language that these are 'research proposal identifiers, not canonical Toledo codes until issue #11') for both the corrected v2 entry and the new v3 entry, so each LINEAGE row is now unambiguously keyed. registry/proposals/flood_outlet_coping.json's own top-level `code` field is UNCHANGED ("weld/M.??.v1") since that string is the established, consistent convention across every sibling PROP-FLOOD proposal in this repo and is not itself a mistake. No claim about the Clay Millennium Navier-Stokes problem, or about any object's Clay/NS status, is made or implied anywhere in this change; the status of every existing Clay-related registry object (CANONICAL.json, coq/canonical/ pre-existing files, docs/CLAY_*) is unchanged.
